exposure: active labor at 6 cm of cervical dilation
active labor at 4 cm of cervical dilation
finding: Defining active labor at 6 cm of cervical dilation, compared to 4 cm, was a cost-effective strategy that reduced cesarean deliveries and improved maternal outcomes, despite a potential increase in adverse neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: This study investigated the impact of changing the cervical dilation threshold for defining active labor (from 4cm to 6cm) on cesarean delivery rates and other maternal and neonatal outcomes.
